stem: What is the distance between two successive crests or successive troughs called?
expl: When a simple periodic wave passes through a medium, the same pattern repeats after a fixed distance (for example, the distance between two successive crests or troughs). This distance is called the wavelength.

stem: The velocity of electromagnetic waves is :

expl: Waves that do not require a material medium for propagation are called electromagnetic waves. Their speed in vacuum is equal to the speed of light, i.e., approximately 3×108 ms-1.

options.text: Can be charged as well as uncharged

expl: Cosmic rays are not a part of the electromagnetic spectrum. They are high-energy charged particles that travel through space at nearly the speed of light.

stem: Which of the following rays are used in the diagnosis of intestinal diseases :
expl: X-rays are a type of electromagnetic radiation. They are used in medicine for the diagnosis of intestinal diseases.

stem: One of the properties associated with X-rays is that they can be deflected by

options.label: a
options.text: Both electric and magnetic fields together

expl: X-rays are electromagnetic waves. They cannot be deflected by electric or magnetic fields because they do not consist of charged particles. They were discovered by Röntgen.

stem: Shrillness of sound is determined by

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Frequency determines the shrillness or pitch of sound. If the frequency of vibration is high, the sound is more shrill and its pitch is higher. If the frequency is low, the pitch is low. Generally, a female voice has a higher frequency and is more shrill than a male voice. It is noteworthy that frequency and wavelength are inversely proportional. Therefore, it is also true that the shrillness of sound depends on its wavelength. For example, the smaller the wavelength, the higher the frequency, and the sound becomes more shrill.

stem: When a sound wave passes from one medium to another, the quantity that remains unchanged is—

options.label: e
options.text: none of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Sound travels from one place to another in the form of waves. A sound wave is a longitudinal mechanical wave. When sound passes from one medium to another, its speed and wavelength change, but its frequency does not change.

expl: Sound waves are called mechanical waves because they require a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas/air) for propagation. In air or gas, sound waves are longitudinal because the particles of the medium oscillate along the direction of wave propagation.

stem: Before playing the orchestra in a musical concert, a sitarist tries to adjust the tension and pluck the string suitably. By doing so, he/she is adjusting

options.label: a
options.text: frequency of the sitar string with the frequency of other musical instruments

options.label: d

expl: Before an orchestra performance, a sitar player tries to adjust the string tension and tune the string properly. By doing so, he adjusts the frequency of the sitar string with the frequency of other musical instruments. Note that equalization is a process used to balance the frequency components within an electronic signal so that it matches the frequency components of other instruments.

stem: A noise level of 100 decibels would correspond to

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: A sound level of 100 decibels corresponds to the noise intensity level of a machine shop. The intensity level of sound is measured in decibels (dB). The World Health Organization (WHO) has fixed the outdoor living-area noise level during daytime at 50–55 dB, while inside bedrooms at night the noise level is 30 dB.

options.label: b

options.label: c
options.text: are sound waves with a frequency between 20 Hz and 20 kHz

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Sound waves with a frequency greater than 20 kHz are called ultrasonic waves. Humans cannot hear this sound; however, some animals (dogs, cat, bat, etc.) can hear it. Ultrasonic waves can be produced using Galton's whistle.

stem: The hearing frequency range of a cat is

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: A cat’s hearing frequency range is approximately 45 Hz to 64 kHz. Note that sound waves can be divided into three categories on the basis of frequency range—Audible waves (20 Hz–20,000 Hz), Infrasonic waves (less than 20 Hz), and Ultrasonic waves (more than 20,000 Hz/20 kHz). Animals like dolphins and bats use ultrasonic waves for echolocation.
